description:
FOUND s484c (Opus, 2026-09-14) by #1727's probe (scratch/s484c/probe/p1727.pl
row 8).  PRE-EXISTING; #1727 changed the two AGGREGATE slots of the same
function and left this one as it was.

perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl:

    sub c { "code" }
    { local *c;
      *c{CODE}     perl undef   PCL undef    agree
      defined &c   perl 0       PCL 1        <-- diverges
    }
    c()  after the scope                     both "code"

CAUSE, located: `%p-glob-clear` (the `local *G` localizer) does
`(when (fboundp code-sym) (fmakunbound code-sym))` and nothing else, while
`%p-glob-clear-code-slot` â the #1020 helper that `undef *G` and `*A = *B`
go through â also does `(remhash sym *p-declared-subs*)`, because
*p-declared-subs* is the OTHER HALF of the code slot, not a cache: `defined
&foo` reads it and a forward declaration (`sub d;`) lives only there.
`%p-glob-restore` already restores that entry (saved slot 8), so the save and
the restore know about the table and only the CLEAR does not.

FIX SHAPE (one line): the remhash, beside the fmakunbound â or better, route
the code slot through %p-glob-clear-code-slot, which is the one reading (it
takes pkg+uname where %p-glob-clear has the symbol, so either the helper
gains a symbol entry point or the localizer gains the pkg/uname it already
has upstream in %p-glob-syms).

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT: the common idiom is `local *Foo::bar = sub {...}`,
which ASSIGNS right after the clear, so `defined &Foo::bar` is 1 either way.
Only the assignment-less `local *c` (temporarily removing a sub) shows it.

BAR: the four rows above plus `exists &c` inside the scope, a forward
declaration (`sub d;` then `local *d`), and the assigning spelling still
answering 1.  A `cl/` change, so the full sweep plus the op/ companion leg.
subject: `local *c` leaves `defined &c` TRUE: %p-glob-clear fmakunbounds the code symbol but does not remove its *p-declared-subs* entry, unlike %p-glob-clear-code-slot
